The villains finally have a hangout spot and now Batman can bring the pain to the Joker instead of all ways trashing his own place.  Imaginext toys are extremely durable. My son just turned 7, so I would say stay in the 3-6 range when purchasing any of the DC Imaginext.  But you really can't go wrong.  I was really happy as a mom who is always plays the villains to have a home base to go to when Batman and his friends are secretly plotting.

Driven by Battat - Dump Truck Vehicle My son has been a huge fan of these driven trucks for some time. We have these full-sized ones, the pocket line, and the micro ones. We've usually bought them at target, but it's wonderful to see that they are now offered on Amazon, since we do much of our shopping here.

These have some simple truck sounds that are not annoying – I've had a lot of different trucks in the past that have played long and irritating songs, so and relieved that this one and all the ones from driven are much more straightforward and truck like in their behavior – and the lights come on. You can lift the dump part to dump things out, and the little back area swings open to allow any Lego bricks, crumpled pieces of paper, etc. to actually fall out easily. All of the driven trucks allow you to move the cab forward, which presumably is how they do maintenance on the machines, but that's one thing that I don't appreciate about any in the driven line, or in some of the other more realistic truck brands. My kids don't really want to play that they are being mechanics, so if the top front part didn't move, that would be just fine with us.

Overall this gets a lot of use in our house, especially in concert with our beloved trash truck.

Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

text_fidelity_a:
Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity It's not wide enough to make a scarf, not for most kids. There is very little yarn included. You will need worsted weight for this kit.

The last point leads into my main issue with this. It does not provide enough information. You know you need yarn, but yarn varies in weight from lace (even gossamer) to super bulky. These terms refer to how thick the yarn is. Buy too thin, and the project will look terrible. Buy too thick and the yarn won't fit into the weft holes. You need worsted weight, and the only reason I know this is I knit and I recognized the yarn. The kit doesn't tell you.

If you hit a knot in the yarn, as I did, you should not keep going. Cut at the end of the row (the instructions don't tell you this) then start on the right side again (the instructions don't tell you this) and whenever you stop or start, leave a tail long enough to weave in later (nothing about weaving in tails is covered -- you're just supposed to know how to do that).

If you want to do the purse, for example, cut 15 strands at 32 inches each (not explained) so that they turn into 16 inch strands when doubled. You can get away with cutting 16 inch and having them single stranded, but it isn't optimal, especially when you are tying pairs at the end. And maybe do it with a yarn not in this kit. They barely provide enough yarn in this kit, and no one wants their kid playing yarn chicken and getting upset. It's cheap yarn. Get a good amount.

When you start the yarn, it is shipped in a center pull ball. While the value of balls is explained a little (I suppose over leaving it in a loose skein or hank to tangle on itself) the concept of center pull isn't touched on. Dig into the ball and get the end inside. That way the ball stays still while you work.

You don't really need the tool to guide the yarn back and forth, but it should have come with a comb to push it down and keep it even, a trick especially hard when you move the piece along down the thread. That's perhaps the biggest design flaw in this. It tends to make the work uneven because it's slid and it leaves gaps where the next section starts. That can mostly be worked out by blocking the piece after (another technique not covered -- wet it, stretch it into the shape you want and even out the rows, and pin it down to dry.)

This is a great kit for someone who already knows a lot about yarn projects like crochet or knitting, or of course weaving. For a first yarn craft, a kid is going to need some help, ideally from someone who knows a lot about yarn projects.
text_fidelity_b: Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity

text_fidelity_a:
Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig UPDATE: Oh, the poor little Bandit! Bandit has been Bingo's security blanket, humping companion, BFF, and "only other dog in the house" until we got a real-live lifewire little dog, Doobie, who is a Jack Chi. Doobie is one high-energy chewing fool. Doobie has gotten up inside of Bandit and pulled his guts out of his butt and also chewed his eyes out, leaving holes. Bingo is not happy and so is trying to tug his dear Bandit away from Doobie, so I knew Bandit was not going to be long for the world. I ordered a new Bandit for Bingo, and he is thrilled, but I'm going to have to put him up until Doobie is over his puppy stage. But this Bandit racoon puppet is a fantastic purchase for a little dog.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Move over Gator. Hit the box, Fox. Bandit has arrived.

Our 10-week-old Chiweenie puppy wants to bite-shake play, and even though he's careful not to be too vicious with DH's hand, he was breaking the skin. I got this puppet as a way to protect us from those sharp little puppy teeth.

Bingo went nuts for Bandit, and we did, too. On my hand, I don't like the fit on my thumb, which tends to slide out of the arm, but it seems to be fine on DH's larger hand. I just lift Bandit by the back and march him up and down, and the puppet is floppy enough, but also firm enough, to seem like a living critter.

I can't emphasize enough how nice the contrast between his nose and white snout is. When we say "bite his nose," he goes right for that little black nose. The nose and the eyes are sewn in very well so I don't worry so much about our dog pulling them off and choking them. Another thing really nice about this puppet is that it has some movement to it even when we are not assisting him in playing with it. He will pick it up and shake it, carry it around like it's his prize possession (which is funny, because it's bigger than he is), and put it in his "room" (a small rug) with his collection of squirrels and such.

UPDATE: Oh, Bandit is such a hit! Bingo sleeps with Bandit, pees on Bandit, madly humps Bandit, chases him all over the house when we throw him, carries him proudly to show "Bingo too" in the mirror, jumps up into the back of the loveseat in the living room with Bandit so Bandit can look out the window with Bingo at the neighbors passing by. Bandit has had to go in the washing machine quite a few times now, and with vicious chiweenie tug-of-war play, poor Bandit's scalp is starting to come unsewn. I can sew him up by hand and he'll be fine, but I'm already thinking I'd better get another Bandit to have on hand for when Bingo's BFF is in complete shreds! Bandit has shrunk some with washing, so it's hard to get a large adult hand into him, but he's still more than doing his job. He and Bingo now are about the same size. Bingo's eight months old and seven pounds.
text_fidelity_b: Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig

text_fidelity_a:
Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players This is a very cute concept and something out-of-the-ordinary for a board game! The object of the game is to make it out with the least amount of goo on your shoe. This is represented by actual pieces of putty that you place on the board and squish with your pawn as you land on a square (thus sticking the goo to your, erm, shoe).
My kids really enjoyed it, but I can't help feeling like there are some design flaws that could have been prevented. For example, the spinner needs to be deconstructed to put away in the box. The way the board folds (see picture), the crease is over the spinner area, and with the bars on the spinner (which I like, as it looks like a playground toy) won't fit, which means you have to totally take that apart and rebuilt it each time. On that note, it isn't much of a spinner at all, but just a wheel. There is no clicker or arrow that sticks out to slow it down as it spins... it basically spins until momentum from your push wears out, sort of like spinning a top. It takes a while to finally stop on its own, which makes the game feel like it is moving slowly. I was very tempted to just stop it manually a few times, but that might bring up the possibility of cheating.
Meanwhile, I wish the goo had more colors, or at least colors that matched the shoes in the game. I can say on the positive note, the goo is very kid friendly!
My daughter lost one of the colors and it turns out she was SITTING on it and it was all stuck in her dress. I suddenly had flashbacks of when silly putty got stuck on her clothing and bed and we had to toss them both because it never came off... but this stuff comes off! It easily rolls into balls with your fingers and comes right off clothing in the process. So, definitely some extra points for that! I just wish the game board and spinner were designed a little better, that would make it a lot more fun to play (and put away!).
text_fidelity_b: Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players

text_fidelity_a:
UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017) This UBTECH JIMU ROBOT-BUILDERBOTS KIT (Interactive Building Block System (357 Piece)) is so beautifully packaged, you’d almost think it was a smartphone or an Apple product. It comes in a heavy-duty, magnetic-closure box that opens like a book. Inside, the main controller, connectors and fasteners are packed in colorful paper boxes that nest perfectly in the big outer box. Is such a lovely unboxing experience wasted on a kid’s toy?

This kit will make either a “Grabberbot” or a “Digbot”. I say “either”, because the building components are extremely hard to take apart--you are NOT going to want to try a rebuild of either completed robot. Some (but not all) of the components are similar to LEGO Technic elements, but they’re smaller and definitely NOT compatible with LEGO.

In an afternoon (about 4 hours), I built the Grabberbot, which I like a lot. Using the Jimu app (iOS or Android), it’s easy to drive, very responsive, and actually picks things up. Grabberbot has a cool, multicolored LED light (you can program custom colors), and he has a voice cube with a large repertoire of sounds (also programmable).

Grabberbot is controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once he’s turned on or plugged into a power source. He does NOT have a separate controller, so you must have a tablet or a smartphone to make him work. (I use an iPad Mini.) It’s a good idea to charge the controller cube before you start building--it takes an hour or so. You do NOT want to spend an afternoon building a robot, and then have to wait for the battery to charge before you can play with it!

You can’t build the Grabberbot without a tablet or smartphone--you have to download the app to get the building instructions. (This is a pet peeve of mine; I believe that the instructions for building toys belong in the box.) However, in defense of the download-only instructions, they are presented in 3D! If you’re unsure about a particular step, you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

Grabberbot is more difficult to build than a motorized LEGO set. There are three reasons for this: (1) the instructions don’t always show the elements recognizably or exactly the way they go together (e.g., the sensor box has fewer connector holes than the one shown in the instructions); (2) the instructions don’t always start at the easiest place for the next step in the assembly; and (3) the components click together so firmly, you need pliers to separate some of them if you make a mistake.

Sadly, the color-changing LED light needs to be programmed if you want it to do more than flash colored lights for a few seconds when Grabberbot is first turned on. I did very little with the programming portion of the app, which requires you to identify which of the four servo motors you want to give instructions to (they are numbered), to choose commands for the motor(s), and to name and record the resulting
action. Programming doesn’t seem to be hard, but it does take some study and practice.

There is a charger with an AC adapter included. The red light on the controller box changes to green when the battery is fully charged. A firmware update starts automatically when you first connect the Grabberbot; it takes only a few minutes.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017)

text_fidelity_a: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+ The toy is well-designed and promises many hours of creative play for my fire-fighter enthusiast grandson. It was easy to put together, with excellent instructions. The construction seems sturdy. I didn't give it five stars because of several factors. I deducted one star for poor paint quality. There were scratches in the paint finish, and the worst were on the header with "Fire Station" painted on it, just where it will be the most visible. The paint seems very thin, and flaked areas look like they'll easily spread with use. In many places, the paint came off when I peeled the part-number stickers off. I deducted the second star because the accessories were not as advertised in the listing or the video. Missing were the doghouse; one of the basketball standards (two were shown; only one was included); the bathroom sink; and one firefighter (two were included; the description promises three). The firefighter's helmet makes it nearly impossible for him to fit through the holes to slide down the pole. The Dalmatian dog pictured was replaced by a brown dog, with a dog bed that he does not fit into, instead of the doghouse. The TV/bookcase console was replaced by a freestanding TV on a pole that is very unrealistic looking. The included accessories match the parts-list in the instruction booklet, so I know the omissions were not accidental.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+

Bomber Lures Who Dat Spoon Spinner Bait Fishing Lure The Bomber Saltwater Grade "Who Dat" Rattling Spinner Spoon - Gold tone from Bomber is a 3" long gold painted spoon like luer with a large 5/0 sized plated hook. It has a guard with a swiveled gold spinner at then end of the plastic and is attached with a screw, which could be removed. When fished for larger saltwater fish, it is a little bit bulkier than the usual spoon, in that is made with a rattling cavity "throat" at the eye end of the body up front to give it a hefty weight forward look. The rattling heard when holding the hook and swivel to keep them from moving is a low pitched clicking rattle. The size of this specific hook is comparable to a 5/0 Strike King hook and it weighed 0.84 ounce on my digital scale. The sound and wobbling, clicking and spinner flash may intimidate a finicky feeding smaller fish, but this luer will only make a big Bull Red Drum hungrier. Big Specs also should not be scared of this spoon and the shiny gold spoon is a proven offering for both redfish and trout. Bomber has offered a uniquely designed product with the Who Dat Rattling Spinner Spoon and the later reviews from buyers will determine if it will catch fish. Good luck with it and enjoy your next day fishing.

Pros:
*Kiddo is 7 and was able to assemble it himself (I helped with the stickers).
*He loved it even if I got bored after about the first 5min. It's super simple and really best for younger kids. Older children will probably tire of the repetitiveness. However, young kids are all about repetition and I think the 4-8 age range is appropriate.
*You can play this solo (as seen in the video) or with 2 players.

Cons:
*The two included trucks are not of equal quality, one is weightier and more metal the other is cheap mostly yellow plastic. You would think they'd have similar trucks since it is head to head.
*The shark is not consistent in what triggers it.
*Either we were terrible or getting just the right force is more skill than it appears. We tended to fling them clear of the arena, oops. Younger kids may get frustrated.
*The stickers are paper and do not allow re-positioning. They tear easily, so get it right the first time or just live with it misaligned.

It's a cute toy, it doesn't actually connect to any other hot wheels sets so consider this a standalone and not an addition. You could snap it apart for storage but I'm not sure what that would do to its durability. Currently is priced around $13 and I think it's a great value $20 may be pushing it though.

All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!

AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

Hot Spot is a fire truck with a really long crane on his hand that you're not supposed to be able to take off, making him awkward to pose as a robot. Once you get him into robot mode, which is no easy feat, you'll have a heck of a time getting him back into firetruck mode. Blades, the helicopter, looks like an awkward chicken when transformed into robot mode, which is not helped by the fact that he appears to not have any hands or arms. The instructions for transforming him were incredibly difficult to decipher, as they have frequent close ups of pieces which I can't really find on my model and curvy arrows pointing at different spots. If a 31 year old with a master's degree can't figure him out, how do we expect a 6-year-old with limited patience to do it?

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min

Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle Monster High toys and accessories are a huge hit with their fan base and the Travel Scaris Convertible vehicle is bound to be a big hit with kids who love Monster High. It is a stylish and attractive toy vehicle with a design that sets it apart from the average kid's toy vehicle.

I'm not usually very impressed with toy vehicles because I have seen so many of them and because most of them look very similar. But this toy vehicle grabbed my attention. The cool, eye- catching, all- around design pattern is one that is bound to warrant a second look and both adults and kids alike will find that it easily stands out against other toy vehicles.

Aside from the exterior, this Monster High vehicle does have other features that make it cool. The stylish wheels glide smoothly across a tile floor or a table without any problem and the vehicle seats up to four Monster High dolls. Rather than have all four dolls face forward, this convertible is a two- seat model with a pair of seats that are actually on top of the trunk, where the dolls face backward. Again, it's something unique that you don't find with other toy vehicles.

The Monster High Travel Scaris Vehicle doesn't have any lights or sounds. This may bother some youngsters, but it is better from an adult perspective because it means no batteries to buy and more imagination required. Most kids will not mind anyway- they will find the vehicle so cool and fun that they will not even notice that it doesn't make noise or have any lights. And another advantage is that boys and girls both seem to like this toy. Girls like it because its Monster High and boys like it because, well, it's a vehicle, which is a toy normally associated with boys.

This Monster High vehicle doesn't have opening side doors, and this is one quality that I wish was different because it would not only look cool, but it would also make it easier to place the dolls into the seats. But other than that, this is a fun, nice- looking toy that belongs in the home of every Monster High fan.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle

VTech PJ Masks Super Learning Headquarters My 4-year-old LOVES this toy. He calls it his "PJ Masks Computer" and wants to play with it constantly. Even when he's not allowed to turn it on (before we leave in the morning), he plays with the vehicles and has a great time. He loves packing it with him in the car, and the sides act as convenient handles for carrying. Do note that the vehicles are not locked down in any way, and are prone to falling off and getting lost if carried around or dumped on the ground in a car tantrum.

Unpackaging the toy is fairly straightforward: you'll need scissors and a screwdriver (or coin). Once you remove it from the box and cardboard packing, you'll find two screws on the back that lock in the Gekko-Mobile and Owl Glider. These unscrew easily with a screwdriver or coin. Catboys vehicle is secured with a zip tie that requires cutting. The toy comes with demonstration batteries (2 AA). They recommend you replace them for full play

The toy is easy to play with. Select your car (character), choose a mode (Vehicle, Science, and Problem Solving) and select a location (Park, Fun Fair, Museum, and Headquarters). There are three activities and four locations, resulting in a total of 12 activities. The games vary and involve avoiding obstacles, sorting items, matching, completing patterns, and learning facts.

This toy is recommended for ages 3-6. Some of the games feel advanced for the younger age range but will give them something to grow into while keeping the 6-year-olds engaged. I'm not sure that my 4 yo really "gets" some of the games, but that doesn't stop him. My 7 yo really loves to play this when she gets a chance.

Like any interactive toy, the volume is higher than necessary. You can adjust the volume (press the volume button, click the car to the left a few times, then click the windshield to set the volume level). Even at the lowest setting, it still feels too loud. It's not too bad if you are a few feet away, or it's in the back seat of the car.
text_fidelity_b: VTech PJ Masks Super Learning Headquarters

text_fidelity_a:
Lost Cities - The Board Game You can move your five explorers (you don't need to use them all) on any of five paths. You can move one square forward on each color if you play a card of that color that is higher than the last card you played. So if you play a two, you can play a three or a four etc, to move forward. You can't play a lower card, but you can discard it, and your opponents can pick it up. Along the way you get bonus points and artifacts to raise your score. Three rounds makes a game.

This game is supposed to take 30 minutes to an hour, but I have yet to find even a three player version go that fast. There is too much strategy and planning involved. You need to think about what cards you need now, what you need later, what your opponents might use if you discard a card, and how many "for later" cards you can retain. You need to decide when to bite the bullet and take a big number jump (limiting your later moves) and when to hold off.

It definitely plays better with more than two players. It's fast to learn, and a lot of fun.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game

When I received this item I was a bit surprised at how large it is, bigger than I expected. I was thinking this would be approximately the size of a bread loaf pan (a testament to how terrible my sense of measure is), so when the box arrived I was surprised when I opened it to find this large plastic truck.

This truck is all plastic which has some pluses and minuses about it. It’s not all that expensive, which would not be the case if it was metal or had metal parts in it. It’s completely waterproof, and it is made well enough to handle some limited abuse. It is not made of heavy-grade plastic, though, so if it is thrown or stood upon it could break.

There are moving parts but everything is manual. No levers, no buttons, no wheels other than the tires, so play isn’t as automated. This may or may not frustrate a young child, though that depends on the child and not the toy. It’s not a toy for the impatient.

This is a decent toy though there are some trade-offs. For the price it is a good unit that will keep a patient child busy. text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4 The idea is great and at $20 (Black Friday) it’s not the worst toy. The problem is that all of the mechanisms are so flimsy that it’s just not a good toy for the age it is meant for. They get frustrated when things don’t work and don’t understand why things don’t work when they take the correct action. Add to that the helicopter mechanism not working at all because it’s too far away from the car, and you just can’t enjoy the toy.

So I mentioned the helicopter doesn’t work. It’s too high for the magnet to grab the car. So your 2 or 3 year old won’t understand at all why one of the knobs doesn’t work. Then the car gets to the bridge, which at least works most often. Then the grey lifting part which constantly comes out of its socket. Then the area where the cars turn…if you aren’t slow and gentle the cars will get bumped off the track. Everything is just so flimsy.

Due to all the issues, as an adult it’s impossible to get a single car all the way through the circuit, even when being as careful as possible. So there’s no way a child can possibly make it happen. Don’t get me wrong, my kid is still playing with it but she doesn’t use any of the buttons or levers…just kinda pushes the cars around the ramp (which comes off every single time she moves the toy)

2 stars because my toddler is enjoying the toy, despite all of its flaws. But none of the things it claims to do…are happening. We will trash this toy in about a week or two.
text_fidelity_b: Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4

text_fidelity_a:
Haktoys RC Quadcopter WiFi HD Live Streaming Drone with Camera, Gesture Recognition, Optical Flow Positioning, Trajectory Plan, Take-Off & Return Key, 360°Flips, Headless Mode We have quite a few quadcopters in our house between my son and I- everything from micro drones that fit in the palm of your hand to foldables and RC car drone combos to full sized DJI Phantoms. So we have a bit of experience with these sort of things, and I have to say I really like this one.
The size is larger than the micro drones but smaller than the RC car combos and a fraction of the pro level ones. This makes it lean enough that we can fly it around indoors but substantial enough to hover and hold it's position properly (the micro drones sometimes shift when a fan turns on LOL). It does all the standard tricks a small Made-in-China drone can be expected to perform, including 360-degree flips, and even includes a surprisingly half decent camera that connects via their app from the play/app store. I mean, its obviously nothing close to my Phantom's camera, and you'd only ever use this for fun and not if you ever want to look at the pictures/video ever again... but it's probably one of the best cheap Chinese drone cameras I've seen yet. Sort of reminds me of a low end cell phone or dash cam in quality, whereas our other cheap drones have horribly grainy/noisy and pixely images with totally wrong and fluctuating color and blown out highlights/darks in any lighting (and one of them even only displays the camera upside-down for some reason- don't ask). The bottom line is, this one is NONE of those things, it's actually pretty decent for a hobby toy.
The ONLY thing I don't like about it, however, is the emergency shut off. Every drone, especially toy ones, need to have one of these features. Think of it like an ABORT button, that you press if something goes wrong such as getting too close to a person or ceiling fan blade, etc, or sometimes in our case if it got stuck somewhere and is about to grind off its propellers into a metal shelf. It is supposed to immediately shut all motors and allow the drone to fall from its position. But the shut off on this remote requires you to press and hold the button for a couple of seconds for it to stop. I thought maybe we were doing it wrong so I checked the instructions again, and sure enough it says "press and hold for a long time". I'm including a shot of the manual page, I couldn't believe it until I saw it. That's a horrible idea for an emergency and would likely be too late if you have to hold the button for a while hoping it stops before the drone damages itself or worse, a person.
So, I want to give this drone 5 stars, I feel like as a drone it is awesome and fantastic. Flies nicely, has great features and a fun camera, but that shut off is a design flaw worth removing at least one star.
text_fidelity_b: Haktoys RC Quadcopter WiFi HD Live Streaming Drone with Camera, Gesture Recognition, Optical Flow Positioning, Trajectory Plan, Take-Off & Return Key, 360°Flips, Headless Mode

LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Clock Tower 75948 Build and Play Tower Set with Harry Potter Minifigures, Popular Harry Potter Gift and Playset with Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger and More (922 Pieces) I’m a massive Harry Potter fan and a massive Lego fan, so naturally I was stalking stores last year, when the first wave of new sets was released. And naturally I’ve been looking forward to another wave ever since.

Coming in at 922 pieces, the Hogwarts Clock Tower is the biggest set in the summer 2019 wave. If you have the other Hogwarts sets (75954: Great Hall and 75953: Whomping Willow), this set can connect to them and make an impressive Hogwarts spread.

There are 8 minifigs in this set: Harry, Ron, Hermione, Cedric, Viktor, Fleur, Dumbledore, and Maxime. Each minifig has a double-sided head. I thought Fleur’s dress bottom was boring, but the detail on Dumbledore and Maxime’s pieces made up for Fleur.

The build itself is pretty simple, no advanced or really interesting techniques. There are 6 numbered bags and 2 sticker sheets. The instructions were in a sort of cardboard pocket built into the box, something I haven’t seen before but appreciated, since I dislike curled or bent pages.

I’ve been dinging Lego on this a lot lately -- but I really wish they used less stickers. Especially for some of the pieces that show up repeatedly in Harry Potter sets, such as the bricks. I decided to assemble this set the first time without applying any of the stickers (I’m quite particular about putting them on perfectly) and it just doesn’t have the same magic without the stickers. Dumbledore’s office is bland without Fawkes and the Sorting Hat in the background. Happily, the clock face is a printed piece.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Clock Tower 75948 Build and Play Tower Set with Harry Potter Minifigures, Popular Harry Potter Gift and Playset with Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger and More (922 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries Big & fast are the best ways to describe this RC racer!

At 1:10 scale, the unit ships with everything you need to run EXCEPT batteries for the RC transmitter. You will need to provide some AA batteries here. Also, make sure to charge your running batteries first.

Unfortunately, you will only get about 10-15 minutes of run time per charge. So having the 2 included battery packs is nice. Although, if you swap them out back-to-back, the one charging will not be ready to go before your second battery depletes. And charge time is roughly 4 hours EACH. So, you actually need A LOT of spare batteries if you want to run your car without any downtime.

Outside of this concern, the car is a lot like a hobby RC vehicle that you would assemble from scratch. But at a fraction of the cost. However, the parts are probably not hobby grade, but good enough for the intended audience of this vehicle.

In the mid-eighties, I was really into RC racing (A Tamiya Frog for those who remember), but even back then this was an expensive hobby (I was around 14, so everything was expensive!) as you always wanted to upgrade something - motor, servos, shocks, tires, etc... And I wasn't even running anywhere near top of the line stuff.

In contrast, this unit ships complete for right around $110.00. So, if you're just getting into the hobby (or re-entering), then this car will make a fun introduction/re-introduction without breaking the bank.

Lastly, this thing is FAST. It's rated right around 30-32MPH. That may seem slow when the only comparison you may have is driving in a car at that speed. However, seeing one of the RC cars rocket down the street at 30+ miles per hour will quickly alter your perspective!

Overall, this is a great out of the box setup that's a ton of fun for a kid, an adult or the kid in every adult!
text_fidelity_b: MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries

There are a lot of little hidden spots all over the board that the images can't show in proper detail, but the variety of plant life hidden inside is spectacular. That means that there are a lot of fiddly plant bits that don't quite have a set rotation or feel to them, so perfectionists might have an issue there.

While these are certainly compatible with LEGO, I found a few inconsistencies. Namely, the small 1x1 flats that dot the floor are a micron or two short, and that left me with a few little gaps that were hard to nudge out. Also, I found that I was missing one leaf piece. Not a big deal, and easily replaceable from our collection.

Neither of these are a huge issue - the checkered floor on the one side is certainly not noticable once everything is in place, but it does go to show that the last second checks may not be there the way they are with the major manufacturers.

Everything was properly labeled, and the instructions were above average for a kit of this size and complexity.

The kit says it should take around 8 hours, I clocked mine at 6 and a half.
